title: Desktop Folder Settings: It's too easy to remove the ability to open the context menu - when it's gone, it's no longer possible to open the settings
line: The Mouse Actions page now warns that removing the Standard Menu action leaves the desktop without a context menu, and how to reopen its settings.
explanation: The Mouse Actions page let users remove the Right-Button Standard Menu action without any notice. Without it the desktop shows no context menu at all, and since the Edit Mode toolbar no longer has a settings entry, users did not know how to get back to these settings. The page now filters its actions for a Standard Menu entry and, when there is none, shows a warning header saying the settings can still be opened with Ctrl+Shift+D while the desktop is focused.

commits.message:
desktoppackage: warn when no mouse action opens the context menu

Removing the Standard Menu mouse action leaves the desktop without a
context menu, which was the usual way back to its settings. Show a warning
on the Mouse Actions page explaining how they can still be opened then.

BUG: 482699

patches.diff:
From ca81a679ed32d4687433ee5fa962efd00060850c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 03:12:21 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] desktoppackage: warn when no mouse action opens the context
 menu

Removing the Standard Menu mouse action leaves the desktop without a
context menu, which was the usual way back to its settings. Show a warning
on the Mouse Actions page explaining how they can still be opened then.

BUG: 482699
---
 .../ConfigurationContainmentActions.qml          | 16 ++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 16 insertions(+)

diff --git a/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/ConfigurationContainmentActions.qml b/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/ConfigurationContainmentActions.qml
index 5cac407e79..66e8eae527 100644
--- a/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/ConfigurationContainmentActions.qml
+++ b/desktoppackage/contents/configuration/ConfigurationContainmentActions.qml
@@ -9,6 +9,8 @@ import QtQuick.Controls as QQC2
 import QtQuick.Layouts
 
 import org.kde.kcmutils as KCM
+import org.kde.kirigami as Kirigami
+import org.kde.kitemmodels as KItemModels
 
 KCM.SimpleKCM {
     id: root
@@ -35,6 +37,20 @@ KCM.SimpleKCM {
         configDialog.currentContainmentActionsModel.save();
     }
 
+    KItemModels.KSortFilterProxyModel {
+        id: contextMenuActions
+        sourceModel: configDialog.currentContainmentActionsModel
+        filterRoleName: "pluginName"
+        filterString: "org.kde.contextmenu"
+    }
+
+    header: Kirigami.InlineMessage {
+        visible: contextMenuActions.count === 0
+        position: Kirigami.InlineMessage.Position.Header
+        type: Kirigami.MessageType.Warning
+        text: i18ndc("plasma_shell_org.kde.plasma.desktop", "@info:status inlinemessage", "Without a Standard Menu action, the desktop has no context menu. These settings can then only be opened with Ctrl+Shift+D while the desktop is focused.")
+    }
+
     Connections {
         target: configDialog.currentContainmentActionsModel
         function onConfigurationChanged() {
--

reviews.text: This is a clean, idiomatic Kirigami fix that directly addresses the usability concern raised by the reporter and developers. Filtering currentContainmentActionsModel with KSortFilterProxyModel for `org.kde.contextmenu` and displaying a warning Kirigami.InlineMessage header immediately informs users when no Standard Menu action remains and documents the Ctrl+Shift+D shortcut to reopen desktop settings. Translations use the proper catalog and context, and the before/after screenshots confirm the warning appears and clears cleanly.

Implements what Nate asked for in c1/c2: a warning while the Standard Menu action is missing, in the right file (the desktoppackage Mouse Actions page), using a KSortFilterProxyModel on the model's real pluginName role and a standard Kirigami header InlineMessage. Since !2695 removed the Edit Mode fallback (c3), naming the remaining way back (Ctrl+Shift+D, the shortcut the desktop containment really sets) is what users need; the after screenshot shows a clear warning that appears and disappears live. Nit: the shortcut is hardcoded in the string, so it goes stale if containments/desktop changes it or a third-party containment reuses the page; reading it from the containment's configure action would be sturdier.
